extraction.name: XTREME-S: Evaluating Cross-lingual Speech Representations
extraction.description: XTREME-S is a new benchmark introduced to evaluate universal cross-lingual speech representations across many languages. It covers four task families: speech recognition, classification, speech-to-text translation, and retrieval. Spanning 102 languages from over 10 language families, 3 different domains, and 4 task families, XTREME-S aims to simplify multilingual speech representation evaluation and catalyze research in “universal” speech representation learning.
extraction.creator: Alexis Conneau, Ankur Bapna, Yu Zhang, Min Ma, Patrick von Platen, Anton Lozhkov, Colin Cherry, Ye Jia, Clara Rivera, Mihir Kale, Daan Van Esch, Vera Axelrod, Simran Khanuja, Jonathan H. Clark, Orhan Firat, Michael Auli, Sebastian Ruder, Jason Riesa, Melvin Johnson
extraction.publisher: Google Research, Hugging Face, Meta AI
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The XTREME-S benchmark aggregates several multilingual speech datasets. It includes a new general-purpose massively multilingual evaluation dataset dubbed Fleurs in 102 languages. For Fleurs-ASR, 2009 n-way parallel sentences from the FLoRes dev and devtest publicly available sets were used, and between one and three recordings were collected for each sentence (2:3 on average). New train-dev-test splits were built with 1509, 150, and 350 sentences for train, dev, and test respectively. Other datasets included are MLS (Multilingual LibriSpeech), VoxPopuli, CoVoST-2, and Minds-14, which are existing multilingual speech datasets.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Physical data collection, Secondary Data analysis
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: The FLEURS dataset is complete at more than 97%. Some slight improvements and changes may be done in a 2nd version of the dataset (e.g., missing recordings, or replaced low-quality recordings).
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Fleurs: 2009 n-way parallel sentences from the FLoRes dev and devtest publicly available sets. MLS: derived from read audiobooks of Librivox. VoxPopuli: semi-supervised learning data from European Parliament sessions. CoVoST-2: a large-scale multilingual speech translation corpus. Minds-14: intent classification task from spoken data extracted from the e-banking domain.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: For Minds-14, monolingual datasets were merged into a single multilingual dataset, with a 30-20-50% train-dev-test split. For the Fleurs speech-text ASR retrieval task, the pool of transcription candidates is augmented with 100k sentences from Wikipedia for each language.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Scripts are provided to download and easily reproduce the preprocessing steps. For Fleurs-ASR, new train-dev-test splits were built. For Minds-14, monolingual datasets were merged into a single multilingual dataset, with a 30-20-50% train-dev-test split.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: For Fleurs-ASR, recordings were collected for each sentence, implying human recording and transcription. MLS is derived from read audiobooks. VoxPopuli includes speech transcriptions and translations. CoVoST-2 is a speech translation corpus. Minds-14 is an intent classification task from spoken data covering 14 intents.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: For speech classification tasks, it is encouraged to re-run fine-tuning several times with different seeds and report the average to minimize variance. Avoiding overfitting on speaker ID for the LangID task is essential for obtaining good performance.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Additional test sets may be added in the future to confirm the generalization ability of submissions. Updates will be made on the HuggingFace platform and XTREME-S Dataset card.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark aims to make speech technology available in all languages, giving speakers of under-represented languages an equal voice on the Internet and the possibility to make their content and culture known outside of their language cluster. It hopes to enable the community to build better speech representations in many languages and provide rapid access to data-efficient speech technology for all the world’s languages.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Results are much better on the Western European group (with 11.5 average WER) than on other groups like Sub-Saharan African (26.7 average WER) or South Asian (20.7). This discrepancy is partly explained by the larger amounts of unlabeled data available in Western European languages from MLS and VoxPopuli. Reducing these gaps across geographical groups is an important research direction.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The tasks are focused particularly on linguistic aspects of speech, while nonlinguistic/paralinguistic aspects of speech relevant to e.g., speech synthesis or voice conversion are not evaluated. Speech classification tasks are prone to overfitting given the discrepancy between the richness of the input signal (speaker, domain, recording conditions) and the small number of output labels. Reducing the gaps across geographical groups is an important research direction.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The benchmark is designed to evaluate universal cross-lingual speech representations. It supports training, testing, validation, and fine-tuning of models, particularly in few-shot settings for low-resource understanding. Usage guidelines include leveraging only the ASR supervision of each task at fine-tuning time (with exceptions for speech retrieval), encouraging the use of publicly available speech and text datasets, and detailing all data used for reproducibility.
